title.zh: 卷一百七十 志第一百二十三 職官十
title.raw: 卷一百七十 志第一百二十三 職官十 Volume 170 Treatises 123: Offical Posts 10

sentences.zh: 舊中書門下、翰林學士、御史中丞並緋衣雙引，仍傳呼。

translations.literal: Formerly, Secretariat chancellors, Hanlin Academicians, and Vice Censors-in-Chief all alike had scarlet-clad double escort, and still had heralds call out.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former regulations, chancellors of the Secretariat, Hanlin Academicians, and Vice Censors-in-Chief alike were preceded by two scarlet-clad attendants, and heralds still called out before them.

sentences.zh: 〈（開寶中，學士止令一吏前導，亦罷傳呼，惟謝恩初上日，雙引傳呼云。）〉

translations.literal: (In the Kaibao era, Academicians were only ordered to have one clerk lead ahead, and calling out was also abolished; only on the first day of expressing thanks for grace did they have double escort and calling out.)
translations.idiomatic: (During Kaibao, Academicians were limited to a single attendant leading the way, and the practice of calling out was discontinued as well; only on the first day when they presented thanks for imperial favor did they again receive double escort and heralds calling out.)

sentences.zh: 使相、僕射、兩省五品已上，一吏前引。

translations.literal: Commissioners with nominal premiership, Vice Premiers, and fifth rank and above in the two central secretariats had one clerk lead ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners bearing nominal premiership, Vice Premiers, and officials of fifth rank and above in the two central secretariats were led by a single attendant.

sentences.zh: 〈（樞密使兼相者，二吏，不讚引。

translations.literal: (Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs who also held premiership had two clerks and no ceremonial announcement.
translations.idiomatic: (A Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs who also held the premiership had two attendants and no herald announcing his passage.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，止令於本廳讚引。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhongxiangfu, they were only ordered to have announcements within their own bureau hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhongxiangfu, announcements were confined to their own bureau halls.

sentences.zh: 不帶相及副使，止令本院紫衣吏前讚引之。）〉

translations.literal: Those not holding premiership and deputy commissioners were only ordered to have a purple-robed clerk from their own bureau lead ahead with announcements.)
translations.idiomatic: Those without the premiership and deputy commissioners were led only by a purple-robed attendant from their own bureau, who announced their passage.)

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，令東宮三少、尚書、丞、郎入朝以緋衣吏前導，並通官嗬止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, it was ordered that the Three Minor Mentors of the Eastern Palace, Ministers, Vice Ministers, and Drafters entering court be led by scarlet-clad clerks, and all had officials shout to halt passersby.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua, the Three Minor Mentors of the Eastern Palace, Ministers, Vice Ministers, and Drafters were required, when entering court, to be preceded by scarlet-clad attendants, and officials were to shout for pedestrians to stand aside.

sentences.zh: 二品已上用朝堂驅使官，餘用本司驅使官，宰臣、親王仍令紫衣一吏引馬。

translations.literal: Second rank and above used court assembly attendants; the rest used attendants from their own offices; chief ministers and imperial princes still had one purple-robed clerk lead their horses.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of second rank and above used attendants assigned from the court assembly; the rest used attendants from their own offices; chief ministers and imperial princes still had a single purple-robed attendant lead their horses.

sentences.zh: 中書、樞密、宣微院、御史臺、開封府、金吾司皆有常從。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Bureau of Palace Attendants, Censorate, Kaifeng Prefecture, and Imperial Guards all had regular retinues.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Bureau of Palace Attendants, Censorate, Kaifeng Prefecture, and Imperial Guards each maintained standing retinues.

sentences.zh: 景德三年詔：「諸行尚書、文明殿學士、資政殿大學士，給從七人；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, an edict stated: "Acting Ministers, Academicians of the Hall of Civil Glory, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue are allotted seven attendants;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde, an edict declared: "Acting Ministers, Academicians of the Hall of Civil Glory, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue receive seven attendants;

sentences.zh: 學士、丞郎，六人；

translations.literal: Academicians and Vice Ministers/Drafters, six;
translations.idiomatic: Academicians, Vice Ministers, and Drafters, six;

sentences.zh: 給事、諫議、舍人，五人；

translations.literal: Drafting Attendants, Remonstrance Officials, and Drafters, five;
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Attendants, Remonstrance Officials, and Secretariat Drafters, five;

sentences.zh: 諸司三品，四人。

translations.literal: Third-rank officials in various bureaus, four.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officials in the various bureaus, four.

sentences.zh: 於開封府、金吾司差借，每季代之。」

translations.literal: They were seconded from Kaifeng Prefecture and the Imperial Guards, replaced each season."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants were seconded from Kaifeng Prefecture and the Imperial Guards and rotated each quarter."

sentences.zh: 中書先差金吾從人，自今亦令參用開封府散從官。

translations.literal: The Secretariat had previously seconded Imperial Guard attendants; from now on they were also ordered to use jointly miscellaneous attendants from Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had previously drawn its attendants from the Imperial Guards; henceforth it was also to employ miscellaneous attendants from Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰臣、參知政事、僕射、御史大夫、中丞、知雜，皆通官嗬止行人。

translations.literal: Chief ministers, Participation Administrators, Vice Premiers, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and supervisory censors all had officials shout to halt pedestrians.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers, Participation Administrators, Vice Premiers, the Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and supervisory censors all had officials call out for pedestrians to stand aside.

sentences.zh: 〈（淳化四年，令東宮三少、尚書丞、郎，並通官嗬止。）〉

translations.literal: (In the fourth year of Chunhua, the Three Minor Mentors of the Eastern Palace, Vice Ministers, and Drafters were all ordered to have officials shout to halt passersby.)
translations.idiomatic: (In the fourth year of Chunhua, the Three Minor Mentors of the Eastern Palace, Vice Ministers, and Drafters were all to have officials call for passersby to stand aside.)

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，以群官導從不合品式，命翰林學士李宗諤、龍圖直學士陳彭年與禮官詳定。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhongxiangfu, because officials' escorts did not conform to rank regulations, Hanlin Academic Li Zong'e and Dragon Diagram Direct Academic Chen Pengnian were ordered together with ritual officials to work out detailed rules.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhongxiangfu, because the escorts of various officials did not conform to rank regulations, Hanlin Academic Li Zong'e and Dragon Diagram Direct Academic Chen Pengnian were ordered, together with ritual officials, to draft detailed rules.

sentences.zh: 宗諤等請：自今除中書、樞密、宣徽使、御史中丞、知雜御史、金吾並攝事清道如舊制嗬導外，僕射已上及三司使、知開封府，止四節；

translations.literal: Li and others requested: From now on, apart from the Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Bureau of Palace Attendants, Censor-in-Chief, supervisory censors, and Imperial Guards—who when acting in office cleared the way according to old regulations with shouted escort—Vice Premiers and above and Commissioners of the Three Departments and Director of Kaifeng were limited to four escort sections;
translations.idiomatic: Li and his colleagues proposed that, apart from the Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Bureau of Palace Attendants, Censor-in-Chief, supervisory censors, and Imperial Guards—who, when acting in office, still cleared the way with shouted escort as under the old regulations—Vice Premiers and above, Commissioners of the Three Departments, and the Director of Kaifeng be limited to four escort sections;

sentences.zh: 尚書、文明殿學士、資政殿大學士，三節；

translations.literal: Ministers, Hall of Civil Glory Academicians, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue, three sections;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, Academicians of the Hall of Civil Glory, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue, three sections;

sentences.zh: 丞郎已上、三司副使，兩節；

translations.literal: Vice Ministers/Drafters and above and deputy commissioners of the Three Departments, two sections;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers, Drafters, and above, and deputy commissioners of the Three Departments, two sections;

sentences.zh: 大兩省、卿、監，一節；

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat officials, ministers, and supervisors, one section;
translations.idiomatic: Senior Secretariat officials, ministers, and supervisors, one section;

sentences.zh: 小兩製御史、郎中、員外、諸司四品，三司、開封府判官推官，二人前行引，不得過五步。

translations.literal: Junior Secretariat censors, bureau chiefs, vice bureau chiefs, fourth-rank officials in various bureaus, and judicial commissioners of the Three Departments and Kaifeng—two men leading ahead, no more than five paces.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Secretariat censors, bureau chiefs, vice bureau chiefs, fourth-rank officials in the various bureaus, and judicial commissioners of the Three Departments and Kaifeng were to have two men leading ahead, no farther than five paces before them.

sentences.zh: 合於金吾借從人者，以諸軍剩員代之。

translations.literal: Those eligible to borrow attendants from the Imperial Guards had surplus personnel from various armies substitute.
translations.idiomatic: Where attendants were to be borrowed from the Imperial Guards, surplus personnel from the various armies were to serve instead.

sentences.zh: 又外任節鎮知州、都監，從軍士七十人；

translations.literal: Also, for prefects and military inspectors of circuit commands on external assignment, seventy soldiers as retinue;
translations.idiomatic: For prefects and military inspectors of frontier circuit commands serving outside the capital, seventy soldiers as escort;

sentences.zh: 通判，十五人；

translations.literal: vice prefects, fifteen;
translations.idiomatic: vice prefects, fifteen;

sentences.zh: 防、團、軍事知州都監，五十人；

translations.literal: military commissioners of defense/training/garrison prefectures and military inspectors, fifty;
translations.idiomatic: prefects and military inspectors of defense, training, and garrison commands, fifty;

sentences.zh: 通判，十人；

translations.literal: vice prefects, ten;
translations.idiomatic: vice prefects, ten;

sentences.zh: 〈（河北、河東、陝西駐泊兵處，節鎮知州、都監百人，防、團、軍事知州都監七十人。）〉

translations.literal: (In Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi where armies were stationed, circuit command prefects and military inspectors had one hundred men; defense/training/garrison prefecture commanders and military inspectors had seventy.)
translations.idiomatic: (In Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi, where troops were stationed, circuit prefects and military inspectors received one hundred men; prefects and military inspectors of defense, training, and garrison commands received seventy.)

sentences.zh: 轉運使，三十人；

translations.literal: Transport commissioners, thirty;
translations.idiomatic: transport commissioners, thirty;

sentences.zh: 〈（咸平二年，詔節度、觀察、防、團、刺史，或別鎮、他鎮，其給使者，止令本使給之。

translations.literal: (In the second year of Xianping, an edict stated that for military governors, observation commissioners, defense/training/garrison commissioners, or commissioners serving in alternate circuits, their allotted attendants were to be provided only by their home commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: (In the second year of Xianping, an edict ruled that for military governors, observation commissioners, and defense, training, and garrison commissioners—whether serving in their home circuit or another—their allotted attendants were to be supplied only by their home commissioner.

sentences.zh: 景德六年，令牧守以州兵隨行者以一年為限。）〉

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingde, it was ordered that prefects taking prefectural troops as escorts be limited to one year.)
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingde, prefects who took prefectural troops as escorts were limited to one year.)

sentences.zh: 副使，二十五人；

translations.literal: Deputy commissioners, twenty-five;
translations.idiomatic: deputy commissioners, twenty-five;

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄官，亦給軍士；

translations.literal: judicial intendant officials also were allotted soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: judicial intendant officials also received soldiers;

sentences.zh: 副留守、節度行軍副使、留守兩使判官，給散從官十五人；

translations.literal: deputy regional commissioners, circuit campaign deputies, and judicial commissioners of regional commissioners were allotted fifteen miscellaneous attendants;
translations.idiomatic: deputy regional commissioners, circuit campaign deputies, and judicial commissioners of regional commissioners received fifteen miscellaneous attendants;

sentences.zh: 小尹、掌書記、支使、防禦、團練副使、兩使推官，十人；

translations.literal: minor prefects, secretaries, branch commissioners, defense/training deputies, and judicial commissioners of the two main circuits, ten;
translations.idiomatic: minor prefects, secretaries, branch commissioners, defense and training deputies, and judicial commissioners of the two main circuits, ten;

sentences.zh: 兩浙推官、防團軍事判官推官、軍監判官，七人；

translations.literal: judicial commissioners of the two Zhe circuits, defense/training/garrison judicial commissioners and commissioners and military supervisors, seven;
translations.idiomatic: judicial commissioners of the two Zhe circuits, defense, training, and garrison judicial commissioners, and military supervisors, seven;

sentences.zh: 錄事諸曹，給承符人；

translations.literal: recorders of various departments were allotted chenfu personnel;
translations.idiomatic: recorders of the various departments received chenfu clerks;

sentences.zh: 縣令、簿、尉、手力、弓手，其代還者，給人護送有差。

translations.literal: magistrates, registrars, constables, clerks and archers—when replaced and returning, escorts of varying numbers were provided.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates, registrars, constables, clerks, and archers—when relieved and returning home—received escorts in varying numbers.

sentences.zh: 賜六劍履上殿，詔書不名，讚拜不名，入朝不趨，紫金魚袋、緋魚袋

translations.literal: Bestowed with the six privileges of sword and shoes in the hall, edicts not using personal name, laudatory bows without personal name, no need to hurry in court, purple-gold fish bag, scarlet fish bag
translations.idiomatic: Bestowal of the six privileges—sword and shoes in the hall, edicts omitting one's personal name, laudatory bows without naming one, exemption from hurrying in court—and of purple-gold and scarlet fish bags

sentences.zh: 右升朝官該恩。

translations.literal: At right: ennoblements eligible to court officials above the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: At right: privileges granted to officials above the court-attendance threshold.

sentences.zh: 著綠二十周年，賜緋魚袋，著緋及二十周年，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: After twenty years wearing green, scarlet fish bag bestowed; after twenty years wearing scarlet, purple-gold fish bag bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years in green robes, a scarlet fish bag was bestowed; after twenty years in scarlet, a purple-gold fish bag was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 〈（特旨者，係臨時指揮。）

translations.literal: (For special edicts, these were temporary directives.
translations.idiomatic: (Special edicts were temporary directives.

sentences.zh: 食邑）〉

translations.literal: fief income households)
translations.idiomatic: fief income households)

sentences.zh: 賜食邑

translations.literal: Bestowed fief income households
translations.idiomatic: Bestowal of fief income households

sentences.zh: 一萬戶、八千戶、七千戶、六千戶、五千戶、四千戶、三千戶、二千戶、一千戶、七百戶、五百戶、四百戶、三百戶、二百戶。
右宰相、親王、樞密使經恩加一千戶，兩府、使相、節度使七百戶。

translations.literal: At right: chief ministers, imperial princes, and Bureau chiefs on periodic ennoblement plus 1,000 households; Two Departments, commissioners with nominal premiership, military governors plus 700.
translations.idiomatic: At right: chief ministers, imperial princes, and Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs received 1,000 additional households on periodic ennoblement; members of the Two Departments, commissioners with nominal premiership, and military governors received 700.

sentences.zh: 宣徽、三司使，觀文殿大學士以下至直學士，文臣侍郎、武臣觀察使、宗室正任以上、皇子上將軍、駙馬都尉加五百戶。

translations.literal: Bureau of Palace Attendants, Commissioners of the Three Departments, Grand Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature down to Direct Academicians, civil Vice Ministers, military observation commissioners, imperial clansmen of regular appointment and above, imperial sons as senior generals, and imperial sons-in-law plus 500 households.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners of the Bureau of Palace Attendants and the Three Departments, Grand Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature down to Direct Academicians, civil Vice Ministers, military observation commissioners, imperial clansmen of regular appointment and above, imperial sons holding senior generalships, and imperial sons-in-law received 500 additional households.

sentences.zh: 宗室大將軍以上加四百戶。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen of great general rank and above plus 400 households.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen of great general rank and above received 400 additional households.

sentences.zh: 知制誥、待制並文臣少卿監、武臣諸司副使、宗室副率已上，並承製、崇班、軍員等，初該恩加三百戶；

translations.literal: Drafters of imperial edicts, academicians-in-waiting, civil junior ministers and supervisors, military deputy commissioners of various bureaus, imperial clansmen of deputy commandant rank and above, and drafters, palace guards, and military staff—on first ennoblement plus 300 households;
translations.idiomatic: Drafters of imperial edicts, academicians-in-waiting, civil junior ministers and supervisors, military deputy commissioners, imperial clansmen of deputy commandant rank and above, and drafters, palace guards, and military staff received 300 additional households on first ennoblement;

sentences.zh: 承製、崇班、軍員再該恩二百戶。

translations.literal: drafters, palace guards, and military staff on second ennoblement plus 200 households.
translations.idiomatic: drafters, palace guards, and military staff received 200 additional households on a second ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 二千戶以上雖有加例，緣無定法，親王、重臣特加有至萬戶者。

translations.literal: Although there were increment rules above 2,000 households, because there was no fixed law, imperial princes and great ministers were specially increased to as many as 10,000.
translations.idiomatic: Although increments were prescribed above 2,000 households, no fixed rule applied; imperial princes and leading ministers were sometimes granted as many as 10,000 households by special favor.

sentences.zh: 食實封：一千戶、八百戶、五百戶、四百戶、三百戶、二百戶、一百戶。

translations.literal: Actual fief households: 1,000, 800, 500, 400, 300, 200, and 100 households.
translations.idiomatic: Actual fief households: 1,000, 800, 500, 400, 300, 200, and 100 households.

sentences.zh: 右宰臣、親王、樞密使經恩加四百戶。

translations.literal: At right: chief ministers, imperial princes, and Bureau chiefs on periodic ennoblement plus 400 households.
translations.idiomatic: At right: chief ministers, imperial princes, and Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs received 400 additional actual households on periodic ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 兩府、使相、節度、宣徽使、皇子上將軍，並宗室駙馬都尉任觀察使已上加三百戶。

translations.literal: Two Departments, commissioners with nominal premiership, military governors, Bureau of Palace Attendants commissioners, imperial sons as senior generals, and imperial clansmen and sons-in-law serving as observation commissioners and above plus 300 households.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Two Departments, commissioners with nominal premiership, military governors, Commissioners of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, imperial sons as senior generals, and imperial clansmen and sons-in-law serving as observation commissioners or above received 300 additional households.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士並宗室正任已上，騎都尉加二百戶。

translations.literal: Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature and imperial clansmen of regular appointment and above, Commandants of Cavalry plus 200 households.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature, imperial clansmen of regular appointment and above, and Commandants of Cavalry received 200 additional households.

sentences.zh: 武臣崇班、宗室副率已上加一百戶。

translations.literal: Military palace guards and imperial clansmen of deputy commandant rank and above plus 100 households.
translations.idiomatic: Military palace guards and imperial clansmen of deputy commandant rank and above received 100 additional households.

sentences.zh: 五百戶已上雖有加例，緣無定法。

translations.literal: Although there were increment rules above 500 households, because there was no fixed law.
translations.idiomatic: Although increments were prescribed above 500 households, no fixed rule applied.

sentences.zh: 親王、重臣有特加至數千戶者。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and great ministers were specially increased to several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and leading ministers were sometimes granted several thousand households by special favor.

sentences.zh: 《三朝志》云：檢校、兼、試官之制，檢校則三師、三公、僕射、尚書、散騎常侍、賓客、祭酒、卿、監、諸行郎中、員外郎之類，兼官則御史大夫、中丞，侍御、殿中、監察御史，試秩則大理司直、評事、秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: The Records of the Three Reigns states: The system of acting, concurrent, and probationary offices—acting offices were the Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, Vice Premiers, Ministers, Regular Attendants, Guests of the Heir Apparent, Libationers, ministers, supervisors, various bureau chiefs, and vice bureau chiefs; concurrent offices were Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Attending, Palace, and Investigating Censors; probationary ranks were Direct Clerks and Reviewers of the Court of Judicial Review and Proofreaders of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Three Reigns states: Under the system of acting, concurrent, and probationary offices, acting appointments covered the Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, Vice Premiers, Ministers, Regular Attendants, Guests of the Heir Apparent, Libationers, ministers, supervisors, and various bureau chiefs and vice chiefs; concurrent appointments covered the Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Attending, Palace, and Investigating Censors; probationary ranks covered Direct Clerks and Reviewers of the Court of Judicial Review and Proofreaders of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 凡武官內職、軍職及刺史已上，皆有檢校官、兼官。

translations.literal: In general, military officials, inner-palace posts, army posts, and prefects and above all had acting and concurrent offices.
translations.idiomatic: In general, military officials, inner-palace appointees, army officers, and prefects and above all held acting and concurrent offices.

sentences.zh: 內殿崇班初授檢校祭酒兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Inner Hall Palace Guards on first appointment received Acting Libationer concurrently with Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Hall Palace Guards were first appointed Acting Libationer and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三班及吏職、蕃官、諸軍副都頭加恩，初授檢校太子賓客兼監察御史，自此累加焉。

translations.literal: Three-Rank personnel and clerical posts, tribal officials, and deputy commanders of various armies on ennoblement first received Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent concurrently with Investigating Censor, and from there were cumulatively increased.
translations.idiomatic: Three-Rank personnel, clerical officials, tribal officials, and deputy commanders of the various armies, upon receiving ennoblement, were first appointed Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Investigating Censor, with further increments added thereafter.

sentences.zh: 廂軍都指揮使止於司徒，軍都指揮使、忠佐馬步都頭止於司空，親軍都虞候、忠佐副都頭以上止於僕射，諸軍指揮使止於吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-Chief of the Garrison Army stopped at Minister of Education; Army Commanders-in-Chief and Loyal Assistants Cavalry and Infantry Commanders stopped at Minister of Works; Commandants and Loyal Assistants Deputy Commanders and above stopped at Vice Premier; various army commanders stopped at Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-Chief of the Garrison Army were capped at Minister of Education; Army Commanders-in-Chief and Loyal Assistants Cavalry and Infantry Commanders at Minister of Works; Commandants of the Imperial Army and Loyal Assistants Deputy Commanders and above at Vice Premier; and commanders of the various armies at Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其官止，若遇恩例，則或加階、爵、功臣。

translations.literal: When their offices stopped, if they encountered ennoblement occasions, they might add rank steps, titles, or merit subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached these caps, further favor might add rank steps, noble titles, or merit subjects instead.

sentences.zh: 幕職初授則試校書郎，再任如至兩使推官，則試大理評事。

translations.literal: Staff posts on first appointment received probationary Proofreader; on second appointment, if reaching judicial commissioner of the two main circuits, then probationary Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Staff appointees were first given probationary Proofreader; on a second appointment reaching judicial commissioner of the two main circuits, they received probationary Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 掌書記、支使、防禦團練判官以上試大理司直、評事，又加則兼監察御史，亦有至檢校員外郎已上者。

translations.literal: Secretaries, branch commissioners, and defense/training judicial commissioners and above received probationary Direct Clerk and Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; with further increments concurrently Investigating Censor, and some reaching Acting Vice Bureau Chief and above.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries, branch commissioners, and defense and training judicial commissioners and above received probationary Direct Clerk or Reviewer; with further increments they might also hold the concurrent Investigating Censor, and some rose to Acting Vice Bureau Chief or higher.

sentences.zh: 行軍副使皆檢校員外已上。

translations.literal: Campaign deputies all had Acting Vice Bureau Chief and above.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign deputies all held Acting Vice Bureau Chief or higher.

sentences.zh: 朝官階、勳高，遇恩亦有加檢校官，郎中則卿、監、少監，員外郎則郎中，太常博士以下則員外郎，並無兼官。

translations.literal: Court officials of high rank steps and merit, on encountering ennoblement also received added acting offices—bureau chiefs received minister/supervisor/junior supervisor, vice bureau chiefs received bureau chief, Masters of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and below received vice bureau chief, and all had no concurrent office.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials of high rank or merit, when ennobled, might also receive acting offices—bureau chiefs up to minister, supervisor, or junior supervisor; vice bureau chiefs up to bureau chief; Masters of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and below up to vice bureau chief—but none received concurrent offices.

sentences.zh: 其解褐評事、校書郎、正字、寺監主簿、助教者，謂之試銜。

translations.literal: Those leaving the brown robe as Reviewer, Proofreader, Regular Scribe, chief clerk of temple/supervisor, and Assistant Instructor were called probationary titles.
translations.idiomatic: Those entering service as Reviewer, Proofreader, Regular Scribe, chief clerk of a temple or supervisorate, or Assistant Instructor were called probationary titles.

sentences.zh: 有選集，同出身例。

translations.literal: They had selection assemblies, the same as regular-entry precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They were listed in selection assemblies on the same footing as regular entrants.

sentences.zh: 兼領者：親祀南郊，則有大禮、禮儀、儀仗、鹵簿、橋道頓遞五使，藉田、泰山封禪、汾陰奉祀、恭上寶冊、南郊恭謝皆如之。

translations.literal: Concurrent appointments: When the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb, there were five commissioners for Great Rites, Ritual, Insignia, Halberd Escort, and Bridge-Road Relay Stations; plowing the sacred field, Feng and Shan at Mount Tai, sacrifices at Fenyin, presentation of the precious register, and Southern Suburb thanksgiving were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent appointments: When the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb, five commissioners were appointed—for Great Rites, Ritual, Insignia, Halberd Escort, and Bridge-Road Relay Stations; the plowing ceremony, Feng and Shan at Mount Tai, sacrifices at Fenyin, presentation of the precious register, and Southern Suburb thanksgiving followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 自餘行禮，或止有大禮、禮儀使。

translations.literal: For other rites performed, sometimes only Great Rites and Ritual commissioners were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: For lesser rites, only Great Rites and Ritual commissioners might be appointed.

sentences.zh: 〈（建隆中南郊，置儀仗都部署、副都署。）〉

translations.literal: (In the Jianlong Southern Suburb, Insignia Chief Deployment and Deputy Chief Deployment were established.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the Jianlong Southern Suburb sacrifice, Chief and Deputy Chiefs of Insignia Deployment were established.)

sentences.zh: 經始大禮，則有經度製置使、副。

translations.literal: When inaugurating great rites, there were Planning and Establishment commissioners and deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When inaugurating major rites, Planning and Establishment commissioners and their deputies were appointed.

sentences.zh: 巡幸，有行宮都部署，行宮有三司使、副使、判官、行宮使、都監。

translations.literal: On imperial tours, there was Chief Deployment of the Traveling Palace; the traveling palace had Commissioners of the Three Departments, deputy commissioners, judicial commissioners, Traveling Palace commissioners, and chief supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, a Chief Deployment of the Traveling Palace was appointed; the traveling palace staff included Commissioners of the Three Departments, deputy commissioners, judicial commissioners, Traveling Palace commissioners, and chief supervisors.

sentences.zh: 舊，南郊止有御營使，咸平中，置行宮使。

translations.literal: Formerly, the Southern Suburb had only an Imperial Camp commissioner; in Xianping, Traveling Palace commissioners were established.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Southern Suburb had only an Imperial Camp commissioner; in the Xianping era Traveling Palace commissioners were added.

sentences.zh: 又有車駕前後、行宮四面、闌前收後、郊壇巡檢巡闌儀仗勾當，編排鹵簿。

translations.literal: There were also commissioners for before and after the imperial carriage, the four sides of the traveling palace, collecting the rear before the barrier, suburban altar inspection and barrier patrol, insignia management, and arranging the halberd escort.
translations.idiomatic: There were also commissioners for the fore and rear of the imperial carriage, the four sides of the traveling palace, collecting the rear before the barrier, suburban altar inspection and barrier patrol, insignia management, and arranging the halberd escort.

sentences.zh: 其百司皆有行在之名。

translations.literal: All the hundred offices had traveling-court designations.
translations.idiomatic: All government offices received traveling-court designations.

sentences.zh: 〈（舊巡幸，百司皆稱隨駕。

translations.literal: (On former tours, all offices were called accompanying the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: (On former tours, all offices were styled as accompanying the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，並同行在某司。）〉

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhongxiangfu, all were changed to traveling-court designations.)
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhongxiangfu, all were renamed with traveling-court designations.)

sentences.zh: 京師居留，則有大內都部署、皇城都點檢、巡檢及增新舊巡檢。

translations.literal: When the capital was left in residence, there were Chief Deployment of the Inner Palace, Chief Inspector of the Imperial City, inspectors, and added new and old inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left the capital in residence, Chief Deployment of the Inner Palace, Chief Inspector of the Imperial City, inspectors, and additional new and old inspectors were appointed.

sentences.zh: 〈（大閱亦置。）〉

translations.literal: (Great reviews also established them.)
translations.idiomatic: (They were also appointed for great military reviews.)

sentences.zh: 征行，則有招討使、招安使、

translations.literal: On campaigns, there were Pacification commissioners and Reconciliation commissioners,
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, there were Pacification commissioners and Reconciliation commissioners,

sentences.zh: 〈（或云捉賊、招安、安撫使名者。）〉

translations.literal: (or so-called Bandit-Capture, Reconciliation, and Pacification commissioner titles.)
translations.idiomatic: (sometimes styled Bandit-Capture, Reconciliation, or Pacification commissioners.)

sentences.zh: 排陳使、都監，前軍、先鋒、大陳、行營、壕砦、頭車、洞子、招收部署、鈐轄、都監，策應之名。

translations.literal: Array commissioners, chief supervisors, vanguard, advance guard, great array, field headquarters, moat fort, lead chariots, covered wagons, recruitment deployment, command oversight, chief supervisors, and responsive-support titles.
translations.idiomatic: array commissioners and chief supervisors, and titles such as vanguard, advance guard, main array, field headquarters, moat fort, lead chariots, covered wagons, recruitment deployment, command oversight, chief supervisors, and responsive support.

sentences.zh: 〈（又有拐子馬、無地名馬，選武幹者別領之。

translations.literal: (There were also hooked-horse units and units without place names; capable military men were selected to command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: (There were also hooked-horse units and units without place names, each led separately by selected capable military officers.

sentences.zh: 親征，則冠以駕前之號。

translations.literal: On personal campaigns, the prefix "before the carriage" was added.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in person, the prefix "Before the Carriage" was added.

sentences.zh: 廉訪民瘼，則有巡撫大使、副大使，字撫使、副使、都監，采訪使、副使。

translations.literal: To investigate popular hardships, there were Touring Pacification chief ambassadors and deputy chief ambassadors, Pacification commissioners and deputies and chief supervisors, and Investigation commissioners and deputies.
translations.idiomatic: To investigate the people's hardships, there were Touring Pacification chief ambassadors and deputy chief ambassadors, Pacification commissioners, deputies, and chief supervisors, and Investigation commissioners and deputies.

sentences.zh: 或官卑者止雲巡撫、安撫，無使字。）〉

translations.literal: Officials of lower rank only said Touring Pacification and Pacification, without the character for commissioner.)
translations.idiomatic: Lower-ranking officials were styled only Touring Pacification and Pacification, without the word "commissioner.")

sentences.zh: 加禮外國，則有國信、接伴、送伴使副；

translations.literal: When extending courtesy to foreign states, there were State Credence, Reception, and Escort commissioners and deputies;
translations.idiomatic: When extending ceremonial courtesy to foreign states, there were State Credence, Reception, and Escort commissioners and deputies;

sentences.zh: 吊祭，大帥若是；

translations.literal: condolence missions followed the same pattern for chief envoys;
translations.idiomatic: condolence missions followed the same pattern for chief envoys;

sentences.zh: 又有翻譯經潤文使，

translations.literal: there were also commissioners for translating scriptures and polishing texts,
translations.idiomatic: there were also commissioners for translating scriptures and polishing texts,

sentences.zh: 〈（宰相為使，以翰林學士為潤文官。）〉

translations.literal: (the chief minister served as commissioner, with a Hanlin Academic as text-polishing officer.)
translations.idiomatic: (the chief minister served as commissioner, with a Hanlin Academic as text-polishing officer.)

sentences.zh: 伸達冤濫，則有理檢使。

translations.literal: to convey grievances of injustice, there were Investigation commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: to convey grievances of injustice, there were Investigation commissioners.

sentences.zh: 勸課農桑，則有勸農使。

translations.literal: to encourage agriculture and sericulture, there were Agriculture-Encouragement commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: to encourage farming and sericulture, there were Agriculture-Encouragement commissioners.

sentences.zh: 講修馬政，則有群牧製置使。

translations.literal: to discuss and reform horse administration, there were Herd-Administration Planning commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: to discuss and reform horse administration, there were Herd-Administration Planning commissioners.

sentences.zh: 最後明堂祫饗，置五使，如南郊。

translations.literal: finally, for the Bright Hall joint-offering feast, five commissioners were established, as at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: finally, for the Bright Hall joint-offering feast, five commissioners were appointed, as at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 其一時特置者，則各具誌傳。

translations.literal: Those established for a time on special appointment each have their own monographic accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Offices established temporarily on special appointment are each recorded in separate monographs.

sentences.zh: 或臨事更製才者，事畢即停。

translations.literal: Some were created ad hoc for immediate needs and ceased when the affair ended.
translations.idiomatic: Some were created ad hoc for immediate needs and abolished once the affair ended.

sentences.zh: 內外名務繁細者，猶不具載。

translations.literal: The numerous and detailed designations at court and outside are still not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The numerous detailed titles at court and in the provinces are still not fully listed here.

sentences.zh: 敘階之法開府儀同三司至將仕郎為文散官，驃騎大將軍至陪戎副尉為武散官。

translations.literal: The method of rank advancement: from Honorary Three Excellencies with Palace Attendance to Aspirant Gentleman were civil honorary offices; from Commandant-in-Chief of Cavalry to Vice Defender of the Army were military honorary offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under the method of rank advancement, Honorary Three Excellencies with Palace Attendance down to Aspirant Gentleman formed the civil honorary ranks, and Commandant-in-Chief of Cavalry down to Vice Defender of the Army formed the military honorary ranks.

sentences.zh: 〈（太平興國元年，改正議大夫為正奉，通議大夫為朝奉，朝議郎為朝奉，承議郎為承直，奉議郎為奉直，宣義郎為通直。）〉

translations.literal: (In the first year of Taipingxingguo, Righteous Discussion Grandee was changed to Regular Supporter, Universal Discussion Grandee to Court Supporter, Court Discussion Gentleman to Court Supporter, Continuing Discussion Gentleman to Continuing Direct, Supporting Discussion Gentleman to Supporting Direct, and Proclaiming Righteousness Gentleman to Universal Direct.)
translations.idiomatic: (In the first year of Taipingxingguo, Righteous Discussion Grandee was renamed Regular Supporter, Universal Discussion Grandee Court Supporter, Court Discussion Gentleman Court Supporter, Continuing Discussion Gentleman Continuing Direct, Supporting Discussion Gentleman Supporting Direct, and Proclaiming Righteousness Gentleman Universal Direct.)

sentences.zh: 京朝官、幕職自將仕郎至朝奉郎，每加五階；

translations.literal: Capital court officials and staff posts from Aspirant Gentleman to Court Supporter Gentleman advanced five steps each time;
translations.idiomatic: Capital court officials and staff appointees from Aspirant Gentleman through Court Supporter Gentleman advanced five steps at a time;

sentences.zh: 至朝散大夫已上，每加一階。

translations.literal: from Court Dispersal Grandee and above, one step was added each time.
translations.idiomatic: from Court Dispersal Grandee upward, one step was added at a time.

sentences.zh: 朝散、銀青者須已服緋紫者。

translations.literal: Court Dispersal and Silver-Green required having already worn scarlet or purple.
translations.idiomatic: Court Dispersal and Silver-Green ranks required that one had already worn scarlet or purple robes.

sentences.zh: 入令錄、判司簿尉，每加一階；

translations.literal: those entering magistrate registers and judicial, clerical, and constable posts advanced one step each time;
translations.idiomatic: those entering magistrate registers and judicial, clerical, and constable posts advanced one step at a time;

sentences.zh: 並幕職計考當服緋紫者，皆奏加朝散、銀青階。

translations.literal: staff posts whose performance review entitled them to scarlet or purple all memorialized for added Court Dispersal and Silver-Green steps.
translations.idiomatic: staff appointees whose performance reviews entitled them to scarlet or purple all memorialized for added Court Dispersal and Silver-Green steps.

sentences.zh: 諸司使已上，如使額高者加金紫階。

translations.literal: Commissioners of various bureaus and above, if their commissioner's quota was high, received added Gold-Purple steps.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners of the various bureaus and above, if their commission carried a high quota, received added Gold-Purple steps.

sentences.zh: 內殿崇班初授則銀青階。

translations.literal: Inner Hall Palace Guards on first appointment received Silver-Green steps.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Hall Palace Guards received Silver-Green steps on first appointment.

sentences.zh: 〈（三班軍職、使職遇恩檢校，兼官，並除銀青階。）〉

translations.literal: (Three-Rank army posts and commissioner posts on ennoblement with acting and concurrent offices all received Silver-Green steps.)
translations.idiomatic: (Three-Rank army posts and commissioner posts, when ennobled with acting or concurrent offices, all received Silver-Green steps.)

sentences.zh: 丁尤者起復，使相則授雲麾將軍，

translations.literal: Those in mourning were recalled to service; commissioners with nominal premiership received General of the Cloud-Banner Regiment,
translations.idiomatic: Those in mourning were recalled to service; commissioners with nominal premiership received General of the Cloud-Banner Regiment,

sentences.zh: 〈（使相仍加金吾上將軍，同正節度使，大將軍同正留後，以下無之。）〉

translations.literal: (commissioners with nominal premiership also received Senior General of the Imperial Guards, equal to regular military governors; great generals equal to regular acting regional commissioners; below that, none.)
translations.idiomatic: (commissioners with nominal premiership also received Senior General of the Imperial Guards, equal to a regular military governor; great generals equaled regular acting regional commissioners; below that, none.)

sentences.zh: 其胥吏掌事而至衣緋者，則授遊擊將軍，千牛備身則授陪戎副尉以上。

translations.literal: clerks in charge of affairs who reached scarlet robes received General of the Mobile Regiment; Imperial Guard attendants received Vice Defender of the Army and above.
translations.idiomatic: clerks in charge of affairs who rose to scarlet robes received General of the Mobile Regiment; Imperial Guard attendants received Vice Defender of the Army or higher.

sentences.zh: 改賜功臣勳官，自上柱國至武騎尉。

translations.literal: Merit subjects and merit ranks were re-bestowed, from Pillar of the State down to Martial Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Merit subjects and merit ranks were re-bestowed, from Pillar of the State down to Martial Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，初敘勳官，即授柱國。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, on first conferral of merit rank, Pillar of the State was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, the first conferral of merit rank had been Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 淳化無年詔：「自今京官、幕職州縣官始武騎尉，朝官始騎都尉，三班及軍員、吏職經恩並授武騎尉。」

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, an edict stated: "From now on capital officials, staff, and prefectural and county officials begin with Martial Cavalry Commandant; court officials begin with Commandant of Cavalry; Three-Rank personnel, military staff, and clerical posts on ennoblement all receive Martial Cavalry Commandant."
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua era, an edict stated: "Henceforth capital officials, staff, and prefectural and county officials begin with Martial Cavalry Commandant; court officials begin with Commandant of Cavalry; Three-Rank personnel, military staff, and clerical officials on ennoblement all receive Martial Cavalry Commandant."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「古之勳爵，悉有職奉之蔭贖，宜以今之所授與散官等，不得用以蔭勳。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Ancient merit titles all had salary and hereditary privilege and redemption; what is now granted with honorary offices and the like may not be used to privilege merit ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "Ancient merit titles all carried salary, hereditary privilege, and redemption rights; what is now granted with honorary offices and the like may not be used to privilege merit ranks."

sentences.zh: 封爵之差，唐制：王，食邑五千戶；

translations.literal: Differences in ennobled titles under Tang regulations: kings, 5,000 fief households;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang regulations on ennobled titles: kings received 5,000 fief households;

sentences.zh: 郡王、國公，三千戶；

translations.literal: princes of commanderies and state dukes, 3,000 households;
translations.idiomatic: princes of commanderies and state dukes, 3,000 households;

sentences.zh: 開國郡公，二千戶；

translations.literal: Founding Duke of a Commandery, 2,000 households;
translations.idiomatic: Founding Dukes of a Commandery, 2,000 households;

sentences.zh: 縣公，千五百戶；

translations.literal: county dukes, 1,500 households;
translations.idiomatic: county dukes, 1,500 households;

sentences.zh: 縣侯，千戶伯，七百戶；

translations.literal: county marquises, 1,000 households; earls, 700 households;
translations.idiomatic: county marquises, 1,000 households; earls, 700 households;

sentences.zh: 子，五百戶；

translations.literal: viscounts, 500 households;
translations.idiomatic: viscounts, 500 households;

sentences.zh: 男，三百戶。

translations.literal: barons, 300 households.
translations.idiomatic: barons, 300 households.

sentences.zh: 又有食實封者，戶給縑帛，每賜爵，遞加一級。

translations.literal: There were also actual fief households, with silk cloth given per household; each ennoblement advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were also actual fief households, with silk cloth issued per household; each new ennoblement advanced one grade.

sentences.zh: 唐末及五代始有加邑特戶，而罷去實封之給，又去縣公之名，封侯以郡。

translations.literal: Late Tang and the Five Dynasties began special additional fief households, abolished grants of actual fiefs, removed the name county duke, and ennobled marquises by commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tang and the Five Dynasties, special additional fief households were introduced, grants of actual fiefs were abolished, the title county duke was dropped, and marquises were ennobled by commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋初沿其制，文臣少監、少卿以上，武臣副率以上，內職崇班以上有封爵；

translations.literal: Early Song followed this system: civil junior supervisors and junior ministers and above, military deputy commandants and above, and inner-palace guards and above received ennobled titles;
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed this system: civil junior supervisors and junior ministers and above, military deputy commandants and above, and inner-palace guards and above received ennobled titles;

sentences.zh: 丞、郎、學士、刺史、大將軍、諸司使以上有實封。

translations.literal: vice ministers, drafters, academicians, prefects, great generals, and bureau commissioners and above had actual fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: vice ministers, drafters, academicians, prefects, great generals, and bureau commissioners and above received actual fiefs.

sentences.zh: 但以增戶數為差，不係爵級。

translations.literal: Only the increase in household numbers served as the difference, not tied to noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Only the increase in household numbers marked the difference, without regard to noble rank.

sentences.zh: 邑過其爵，則並進爵焉，止於郡公。

translations.literal: When the fief exceeded one's title, the title was advanced together, stopping at Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the fief exceeded one's title, the title was advanced as well, up to Duke of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 每加食邑，自千戶至二百戶，實封自六百戶至百戶。

translations.literal: Each addition to fief income ran from 1,000 to 200 households; actual fiefs from 600 to 100 households.
translations.idiomatic: Each addition to fief income ran from 1,000 down to 200 households; actual fiefs from 600 down to 100 households.

sentences.zh: 親王、重臣或特加，有逾千戶者。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and great ministers might be specially increased, some exceeding 1,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and leading ministers might receive special increases, some exceeding 1,000 households.

sentences.zh: 〈（郡公食邑有累加至萬餘，實封至數千戶者。）〉

translations.literal: (Dukes of commanderies' fief income could cumulatively reach over 10,000; actual fiefs reached several thousand households.)
translations.idiomatic: (Dukes of commanderies' fief income could cumulatively exceed 10,000 households; actual fiefs could reach several thousand.)

sentences.zh: 皇屬特封郡公、縣公或贈侯者，無「開國」字。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen specially ennobled as dukes of commanderies or county dukes, or posthumously granted marquis, had no "Founding" character.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen specially ennobled as dukes of commanderies or county dukes, or posthumously granted marquis, bore no "Founding" in the title.

sentences.zh: 〈（侯亦在開國郡公之上。）〉

translations.literal: (Marquis also ranked above Founding Duke of a Commandery.)
translations.idiomatic: (Marquis also ranked above Founding Duke of a Commandery.)

sentences.zh: 又采秦製賜爵曰「公士」。

translations.literal: The Qin system was also adopted to bestow the title "Gentleman of the State."
translations.idiomatic: The Qin practice was also adopted to bestow the title Gentleman of the State.

sentences.zh: 〈（端拱二年，賜諸州高年一百二十七人爵公士，景德中，福建民有擒獲強盜者，當授鎮將，以遠俗非所樂，並賜公士，自後率為例。）〉

translations.literal: (In the second year of Duangong, 127 elderly persons in various prefectures were granted the title Gentleman of the State; in Jingde, Fujian commoners who captured bandits were to receive garrison general, but because distant customs did not favor it, all were granted Gentleman of the State, and thereafter this became the precedent.)
translations.idiomatic: (In the second year of Duangong, 127 elderly persons in various prefectures were granted Gentleman of the State; in Jingde, Fujian commoners who captured bandits were to receive garrison general, but because frontier custom disfavored it, all were granted Gentleman of the State instead, and thereafter this became precedent.)

sentences.zh: 功臣者，唐開元間賜號「開元功臣」，代宗時有「寶應功臣」，德宗時有「奉天定難元從功臣」之號，僖宗將相多加功臣美名，五代浸增其制。

translations.literal: Merit subjects: in Tang Kaiyuan they were granted the title "Kaiyuan Merit Subject"; in Daizong's time there was "Baoying Merit Subject"; in Dezong's time the title "Merit Subject Original Follower Who Settled Heaven and Quelled Difficulty"; in Xizong's time generals and ministers often added fine merit-subject names; the Five Dynasties gradually expanded the system.
translations.idiomatic: Merit subjects: in Tang Kaiyuan they received the title Kaiyuan Merit Subject; under Daizong, Baoying Merit Subject; under Dezong, Merit Subject, Original Follower Who Pacified Heaven and Quelled Crisis; under Xizong, generals and ministers often added elaborate merit-subject epithets; the Five Dynasties gradually expanded the system.

sentences.zh: 宋初因之，凡宣製而授者，多賜焉。

translations.literal: Early Song followed this; those proclaimed and appointed by edict were mostly granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed this practice; those proclaimed and appointed by edict were usually granted merit subjects.

sentences.zh: 參知政事、樞密副使、刺史以上階、勳高者亦賜之。

translations.literal: Participation Administrators, Deputy Bureau chiefs, prefects and above in rank steps, and those of high merit also received them.
translations.idiomatic: Participation Administrators, Deputy Bureau chiefs, prefects and above in rank, and those of high merit also received them.

sentences.zh: 中書、樞密則「推忠」、協謀，親王則「崇仁、「佐運」，餘官則「推誠」，「保德」、「翊戴」，掌兵則「忠果」、「雄勇」、「宣力」，外臣則「純誠」、「順化」。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs received "Loyal in Advancement" and "Cooperating in Planning"; imperial princes "Honoring Benevolence" and "Assisting the Mandate"; other officials "Sincere in Advancement," "Preserving Virtue," and "Supporting the Throne"; those commanding troops "Loyal and Fruitful," "Heroic and Brave," and "Proclaiming Strength"; outer officials "Purely Sincere" and "Following Transformation."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs received Loyal in Advancement and Cooperating in Planning; imperial princes Honoring Benevolence and Assisting the Mandate; other officials Sincere in Advancement, Preserving Virtue, and Supporting the Throne; commanders Loyal and Fruitful, Heroic and Brave, and Proclaiming Strength; frontier officials Purely Sincere and Following Transformation.

sentences.zh: 宰相初加即六字，餘並四安，其累加則二字，中書、樞密所賜，若罷免或出鎮，則改之。

translations.literal: Chief ministers on first addition received six characters; the rest all four characters; cumulative additions were two characters; those granted by the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, if dismissed or sent out to command a circuit, were changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers on first appointment received six-character titles; the rest four characters; cumulative additions two characters; titles granted by the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs were changed if the holder was dismissed or sent out to command a circuit.

sentences.zh: 其諸班直將士禁軍，則賜「拱衛」、「翊衛」等號，遇恩累加，但改其名，不過兩字。

translations.literal: Various rank-and-file generals and soldiers of the imperial guard received titles such as "Arch-Guard" and "Flank-Guard"; on repeated favor only the name was changed, not exceeding two characters.
translations.idiomatic: Rank-and-file generals and soldiers of the imperial guard received titles such as Arch-Guard and Flank-Guard; on repeated favor only the epithet changed, never exceeding two characters.

sentences.zh: 宋制，設祠祿之官，以佚老優賢。

translations.literal: Under Song regulations, sacrificial-salary offices were established to give repose to the aged and honor the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song regulations, sacrificial-salary offices were established to provide for retired elders and honor the worthy.

sentences.zh: 先時員數絕少，熙寧以後乃增置焉。

translations.literal: Formerly the number of posts was extremely few; after Xining they were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the number of posts was very small; after the Xining reforms they were greatly increased.

sentences.zh: 在京宮觀，舊制以宰相、執政充使，或丞、郎、學士以上充副使，兩省或五品以上為判官，內侍官或諸司使、副

translations.literal: For capital palace abbeys, the old system had chief ministers and administrators serve as commissioners, or vice ministers, drafters, and academicians and above as deputy commissioners, two secretariats or fifth rank and above as judicial commissioners, eunuchs or bureau commissioners and deputies
translations.idiomatic: For capital palace abbeys, the old system appointed chief ministers and administrators as commissioners, vice ministers, drafters, and academicians and above as deputy commissioners, officials of the two secretariats or fifth rank and above as judicial commissioners, and eunuchs or bureau commissioners and deputies

sentences.zh: 〈（政和改武臣官制，以使為大夫，以副使為郎。）〉

translations.literal: (In Zhenghe the military official system was changed, commissioners becoming grandees and deputy commissioners gentlemen.)
translations.idiomatic: (In Zhenghe the military official system was revised, with commissioners becoming grandees and deputy commissioners gentlemen.)

sentences.zh: 為都監，又有提舉、提點、主管。

translations.literal: as chief supervisors; there were also overseers, inspectors, and managers.
translations.idiomatic: as chief supervisors; there were also overseers, inspectors, and managers.

sentences.zh: 其戚裏、近屬及前宰執留京師者，多除宮觀，以示優禮。

translations.literal: Imperial affines, close kin, and former chief ministers remaining in the capital were mostly given palace abbey posts to show special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial affines, close kin, and former chief ministers who remained in the capital were often given palace abbey posts as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方經理時政，患疲老不任事者廢職，欲悉罷之。

translations.literal: At the time the court was reorganizing current administration, fearing that the feeble and aged who could not handle affairs were wasting posts and wishing to dismiss them all.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was reorganizing administration and wished to dismiss all feeble and aged officials who could no longer perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 乃使任宮觀，以食其祿。

translations.literal: They were therefore assigned to palace abbeys to receive their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: They were therefore assigned to palace abbeys so they could continue to receive their salaries.

sentences.zh: 王安石亦欲以此處異議者，遂詔：「宮觀毋限員。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi also wished to place dissenters in such posts, and thus an edict stated: "Palace abbeys are not limited in quota.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi also wished to place dissenters in such posts, and thus an edict declared: "Palace abbeys are not limited in quota.

sentences.zh: 並差知州資序人。

translations.literal: All are to be assigned persons of prefectural commissioner qualification.
translations.idiomatic: All appointees must be of prefectural commissioner qualification.

sentences.zh: 以三十月為任。」

translations.literal: A term of thirty months is set."
translations.idiomatic: The term is set at thirty months."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「杭州洞霄宮、亳州明道宮、華州雲台觀、建州武夷觀、台州崇道觀、成都玉局觀、建昌軍仙都觀、江州太平觀、洪州玉隆觀、五嶽廟自今並依嵩山崇福宮、舒州靈仙觀置管幹或提舉、提點官。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "From now on Hangzhou Cave of Heaven Abbey, Bozhou Bright Way Abbey, Huazhou Cloud Terrace Abbey, Jianzhou Wuyi Abbey, Taizhou Honoring the Way Abbey, Chengdu Jade Bureau Abbey, Jianchang Commandery Immortal Capital Abbey, Jiangzhou Great Peace Abbey, Hongzhou Jade Prosperity Abbey, and the Five Sacred Peak temples shall all, following Mount Song Blessedness Abbey and Shuzhou Spirit Immortal Abbey, establish managing, overseeing, or inspecting officials."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered that henceforth the Cave of Heaven Abbey at Hangzhou, Bright Way Abbey at Bozhou, Cloud Terrace Abbey at Huazhou, Wuyi Abbey at Jianzhou, Honoring the Way Abbey at Taizhou, Jade Bureau Abbey at Chengdu, Immortal Capital Abbey at Jianchang Commandery, Great Peace Abbey at Jiangzhou, Jade Prosperity Abbey at Hongzhou, and the Five Sacred Peak temples—all following Mount Song Blessedness Abbey and Shuzhou Spirit Immortal Abbey—establish managing, overseeing, or inspecting officials."

sentences.zh: 「奉給，大兩省、卿、監及職司資序人視小郡知州，知州資序人視小郡通判，武臣仿此。」

translations.literal: "Salaries: grand secretariat officials, ministers, supervisors, and functional-post qualification persons are treated as prefects of small commanderies; prefectural commissioner qualification persons as vice prefects of small commanderies; military officials follow this pattern."
translations.idiomatic: "Salaries: grand secretariat officials, ministers, supervisors, and functional-post qualification holders receive the salary of a small-commandery prefect; prefectural commissioner qualification holders that of a small-commandery vice prefect; military officials follow the same pattern."

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「宮觀、嶽廟留官一員，餘聽如分司、致仕例，從便居住。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict stated: "Palace abbeys and peak temples keep one official on duty; the rest may follow the precedent for branch-service and retirement, residing where convenient."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an edict stated: "Each palace abbey and peak temple keeps one official on duty; the rest may follow branch-service and retirement precedent and reside where convenient."

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：「卿、監、職司以上提舉，餘官管幹。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict stated: "Ministers, supervisors, and functional posts and above serve as overseers; other officials as managers."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict stated: "Ministers, supervisors, and functional posts and above serve as overseers; other officials as managers."

sentences.zh: 又有以京官為幹當者。

translations.literal: There were also capital officials appointed as handlers.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials were also appointed as handlers.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「年六十以上者乃聽差，毋過兩任。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Only those sixty and above may be assigned, not exceeding two terms.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "Only those sixty and above may be assigned, not exceeding two terms.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「兼用執政恩例者，通不得過三任。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "Those also using administrator favor precedent may not exceed three terms in total."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "Those also using administrator favor precedent may not exceed three terms in total."

sentences.zh: 元豐中，王安石以左僕射、觀文殿大學士為集禧觀使，呂公著、韓維以資政殿學士兼侍讀、仍提舉中太一宮兼集禧觀公事。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng, Wang Anshi as Left Vice Premier and Grand Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature became commissioner of the Abbey of Gathered Blessings; Lü Gongzhu and Han Wei as Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue concurrently Readers still oversaw the Central Great Unity Palace and Abbey of Gathered Blessings affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng, Wang Anshi, as Left Vice Premier and Grand Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature, became commissioner of the Abbey of Gathered Blessings; Lü Gongzhu and Han Wei, as Academicians of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue and concurrent Readers, continued to oversee the Central Great Unity Palace and Abbey of Gathered Blessings.

sentences.zh: 元祐間，馮京以觀文殿學士、梁燾以資政殿學士為中太一宮、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou, Feng Jing as Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Liang Tao as Academic of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue became commissioners of the Central Great Unity Palace and Sweet Spring Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou, Feng Jing, as Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and Liang Tao, as Academic of the Hall for Cherishing Virtue, became commissioners of the Central Great Unity Palace and Sweet Spring Abbey.

sentences.zh: 範鎮落致仕，以端明殿學士提舉中太一宮兼集禧觀公事。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen left retirement and as Academic of the Bright Hall oversaw the Central Great Unity Palace and Abbey of Gathered Blessings affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen left retirement and, as Academic of the Bright Hall, oversaw the Central Great Unity Palace and Abbey of Gathered Blessings.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔：「橫行使、副無兼領者，許兼宮觀一處。」」

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict stated: "Horizontal-rank commissioners and deputies without concurrent posts may hold one palace abbey concurrently."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict stated: "Horizontal-rank commissioners and deputies without concurrent posts may hold one palace abbey concurrently."

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：「橫行狄諮、宋球既領皇城司，罷提點醴泉觀。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict stated: "Horizontal-rank Di Zhe and Song Qiu, having taken charge of the Imperial City Bureau, are dismissed from inspecting Sweet Spring Abbey."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict stated: "Horizontal-rank Di Zhe and Song Qiu, having taken charge of the Imperial City Bureau, are relieved of inspection duty at Sweet Spring Abbey."

sentences.zh: 元符元年，高遵固年八十一，乞再任宮觀，高遵禮年七十六，乞再任亳州太清宮，又從其再任之請，以待遇宣仁親屬故也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Gao Zungu at age eighty-one requested another palace abbey term; Gao Zunli at seventy-six requested another term at Bozhou Great Purity Palace; their requests for reappointment were granted because of treatment due to Empress Dowager Xuanren's kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfu, Gao Zungu, aged eighty-one, requested another palace abbey term; Gao Zunli, aged seventy-six, requested another term at the Great Purity Palace in Bozhou; both requests were granted because of favors owed to Empress Dowager Xuanren's kin.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，趙挺之以觀文殿大學士為佑神觀使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, Zhao Tingzhi as Grand Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature became commissioner of the Abbey for Assisting the Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan, Zhao Tingzhi, as Grand Academic of the Hall for Viewing Literature, became commissioner of the Abbey for Assisting the Spirits.

sentences.zh: 政和六年詔。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, an edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, an edict stated:

sentences.zh: 「措置宮觀，如萬壽、醴泉近百員，更不立額。」

translations.literal: "In arranging palace abbeys, such as Longevity and Sweet Spring, nearly a hundred posts—no further quotas are to be established."
translations.idiomatic: "In arranging palace abbeys such as Longevity and Sweet Spring, nearly a hundred posts exist—no further quotas are to be established."

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔內外官見帶提舉、主管神霄玉清萬壽宮並罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict abolished all inner and outer officials currently holding oversight or management of the Divine Empyrean Jade Clarity Longevity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict abolished all posts held by inner and outer officials as overseers or managers of the Divine Empyrean Jade Clarity Longevity Palace.

sentences.zh: 大抵祠館之設，均為佚老優賢，而有內外之別，京祠以前宰相、見任使相充使，次充提舉；

translations.literal: In general, the establishment of shrine posts was all to give repose to the aged and honor the worthy, with distinctions between inner and outer; capital shrines had former chief ministers and current commissioners with nominal premiership serve as commissioners, next as overseers;
translations.idiomatic: In general, shrine posts were established to provide for retired elders and honor the worthy, with inner and outer distinctions; capital shrines appointed former chief ministers and current commissioners with nominal premiership as commissioners, and next as overseers;

sentences.zh: 餘則為提點，為主管，皆隨官之高下，處以外祠。

translations.literal: the rest served as inspectors or managers, all according to the height of office, placed in outer shrines.
translations.idiomatic: the rest served as inspectors or managers according to rank, in outer shrines.

sentences.zh: 選人為監嶽廟，非自陳而朝廷特差者，如黜降之例。

translations.literal: Selectees supervising peak temples, when not self-petitioning but specially assigned by the court, were treated like demotion cases.
translations.idiomatic: Selectees appointed to supervise peak temples, when not self-petitioning but specially assigned by the court, were treated like demotions.

sentences.zh: 紹興以來，士大夫多流離，困厄之餘，未有闕以處之。

translations.literal: Since Shaoxing, many scholar-officials were displaced; after hardship there were no vacancies to place them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaoxing, many scholar-officials were displaced; after their hardships there were no vacancies to place them.

sentences.zh: 於是許以承務郎以上權差宮觀一次，續又有選人在部無闕可入與破格嶽廟者，亦有以宰執恩例陳乞而與之者，月破供給。

translations.literal: Therefore those of Gentleman for Service Assistance and above were permitted one provisional palace abbey assignment; later there were also selectees in the capital with no vacancy to enter and exceptional peak-temple appointments, and some who petitioned using administrator favor precedent and received them, with monthly allowances drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore officials of Gentleman for Service Assistance and above were permitted one provisional palace abbey assignment; later selectees in the capital with no vacancy, exceptional peak-temple appointments, and petitioners using administrator favor precedent also received posts, with monthly allowances.

sentences.zh: 〈（非責降官並月破供給，依資序降二等支。）〉

translations.literal: (Those not demoted on disciplinary grounds also drew monthly allowances, paid two grades below their qualification.)
translations.idiomatic: (Those not demoted on disciplinary grounds also drew monthly allowances, paid two grades below their qualification.)

sentences.zh: 理為資任，意至厚也。

translations.literal: Treating this as qualifying service showed intent of great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Counting such service toward qualification showed extraordinary generosity.

sentences.zh: 然初將以撫安不調之人，末乃重僥求泛與之弊。

translations.literal: Yet what began as pacifying maladjusted persons in the end heavily emphasized the abuses of importunate requests and indiscriminate grants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what began as a means to pacify maladjusted officials in the end fostered importunate requests and indiscriminate grants.

sentences.zh: 於是臣僚交章，欲罷供給以絕幹請，變理任以抑僥幸，嚴按格以去泛濫。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials submitted successive memorials, wishing to abolish allowances to cut off importunate requests, change how qualifying service was counted to restrain undeserved favor, and strictly apply regulations to remove indiscriminate grants.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials submitted memorial after memorial, seeking to abolish allowances and thereby end importunate requests, revise how qualifying service was counted to check opportunistic gain, and enforce regulations strictly to curb indiscriminate grants.

sentences.zh: 上並從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，稍復祖宗條法之舊。

translations.literal: From then on, the ancestral regulations were somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the regulations of the founding ancestors were gradually restored.

sentences.zh: 又有年及七十，耄昏不堪牧養而不肯自陳宮觀者，復申明舊法，著為定令以律之。

translations.literal: There were also those who reached seventy, were senile and dim and unfit to govern the people yet would not petition for palace abbey posts; the old law was again clarified and established as fixed regulation to discipline them.
translations.idiomatic: There were also officials who reached seventy, were senile and unfit to govern yet refused to petition for palace abbey posts; the old law was reaffirmed and written into fixed regulation to enforce compliance.

sentences.zh: 〈（舊制，六十以上知州資序人，本部長官體量精神不致昏昧堪厘務者，許差一任，兼用執政官陳乞者加一任。

translations.literal: (Former regulation: for those sixty and above qualified by seniority for prefect, if the chief of their circuit measured their spirit and found them not dim but able to manage affairs, one assignment was permitted; if administrators petitioned on their behalf, one additional assignment was added.
translations.idiomatic: (Under the former regulation, prefectural appointees sixty and above who, upon review by their circuit chief, were found still clear-minded and fit to manage affairs were permitted one assignment; if an administrator petitioned on their behalf, one further assignment was added.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十二年，臣僚言：「郡守之職，其任至重，昨朝廷以年及七十，令吏部與自陳宮觀，乞將前項指揮永為著令。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Shaoxing, officials said: "The post of prefect is extremely weighty. Yesterday the court, for those reaching seventy, ordered the Ministry of Personnel to allow self-petition for palace abbeys. We ask that the above directive be permanently established as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Shaoxing, officials said: "The office of prefect carries immense responsibility. Recently the court, for those reaching seventy, ordered the Ministry of Personnel to permit self-petition for palace abbeys. We ask that this directive be permanently codified."

sentences.zh: 從之。）〉

translations.literal: Approved.)
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.)

sentences.zh: 蓋不當請而請，則冗瑣者流競竊優閑廩稍；

translations.literal: For if one petitioned when one should not, the trivial would compete to seize leisurely allowances;
translations.idiomatic: For when one petitioned though unqualified, the unworthy would rush to seize comfortable stipends;

sentences.zh: 或當請而不請，則知進而不知退，識者羞焉。

translations.literal: or if one should petition but did not, one knew advance but not retreat—the discerning were ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: and when one ought to petition but did not, one knew how to advance but not how to withdraw—a shame to the discerning.

sentences.zh: 一祠館之與奪，不可不謹如是。

translations.literal: The granting and withholding of shrine posts must be watched this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The granting and withholding of shrine posts had to be handled with such care.

sentences.zh: 故重內祠，專使職，所以崇大臣之體貌，一次以定法，再任以示恩，

translations.literal: Therefore inner shrines were weighted, commissioner posts specialized, to honor the dignity of great ministers—one term by fixed law, a second to show favor,
translations.idiomatic: Therefore inner shrines were emphasized and commissioner posts reserved, to uphold the ceremonial stature of great ministers—one term by fixed rule, a second to show imperial favor,

sentences.zh: 〈（紹熙五年慶壽赦，應文武臣宮觀、嶽廟已滿，不應再陳者，該今來慶壽恩，年八十以上，特許更陳一次。）〉

translations.literal: (In the Longevity Celebration amnesty of the fifth year of Shaoxi, for civil and military officials whose palace abbey or peak temple terms were complete and who should not petition again—under this Longevity Celebration grace, those eighty and above were specially permitted one further petition.)
translations.idiomatic: (In the Longevity Celebration amnesty of the fifth year of Shaoxi, civil and military officials whose palace abbey or peak temple terms were complete and who should not have petitioned again were, under this Longevity Celebration grace, specially permitted one further petition if eighty or older.)

sentences.zh: 京官以上二年，選人三年，凡待庶僚者，皆於優厚之中寓閑製之意焉。

translations.literal: Capital officials two years, selectees three years—for all awaiting ordinary subordinates, all contained within generosity the intent of leisure restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials served two years, selectees three; for all who awaited ordinary subordinates, generosity was tempered by an intent to restrain idleness.

sentences.zh: 建隆已來，凡有恩例，文武朝官、諸司使副、禁軍及藩方馬步都指揮使以上，父亡皆贈官。

translations.literal: Since Jianlong, in all favor cases, civil and military court officials, deputy commissioners of various bureaus, palace army and frontier cavalry and infantry commanders-in-chief and above—all received posthumous offices when fathers died.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jianlong, whenever favor was granted, civil and military court officials, deputy commissioners of various bureaus, and palace army and frontier cavalry and infantry commanders-in-chief and above all received posthumous offices upon their fathers' deaths.

sentences.zh: 親王贈三官，可贈者贈二官，追加大國。

translations.literal: Imperial princes received three posthumous offices; those eligible received two, with promotion to great state.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes received three posthumous offices; those eligible for ennoblement received two, with promotion to a great state.

sentences.zh: 皇屬近親如之。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen of close kinship likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen of close kinship were treated likewise.

sentences.zh: 追加封爵。

translations.literal: With additional ennoblement titles.
translations.idiomatic: Additional noble titles were also conferred.

sentences.zh: 服疏及諸親之服近者贈一官。

translations.literal: Those submitting mourning reports and those in mourning for close relatives received one posthumous office.
translations.idiomatic: Those submitting mourning reports and those mourning close relatives received one posthumous office.

sentences.zh: 宰相、樞密使贈二官。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and Bureau chiefs received two posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs received two posthumous offices.

sentences.zh: 使相、參知政事、樞密副使、尚書已上、三司使、節度使、留後、觀察使、統軍上將軍、內臣任都知副都知者，贈一官。

translations.literal: Commissioners with nominal premiership, Vice Grand Councillors, Vice Bureau chiefs, Vice Ministers and above, Commissioners of the Three Departments, military governors, acting governors, observation commissioners, senior army commanders, and eunuchs serving as chief or deputy chief—all received one posthumous office.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners with nominal premiership, Vice Grand Councillors, Vice Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Ministers and above, Commissioners of the Three Departments, military governors, acting governors, observation commissioners, senior army commanders, and eunuchs serving as chief or deputy chief all received one posthumous office.

sentences.zh: 此皇族及臣僚薨卒贈官之法也。

translations.literal: This was the law for posthumous offices when imperial clansmen and officials died.
translations.idiomatic: This was the law governing posthumous offices for deceased imperial clansmen and officials.

sentences.zh: 其官秩未至，而因勳舊褒錄或沒王事，雖卑秩皆贈官加等者，並係臨時取旨。

translations.literal: When rank had not yet been reached but merit or dying in imperial service led to posthumous offices with added grades even from humble rank—all depended on temporary imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: When an official's rank had not yet qualified but meritorious service or death in imperial service warranted posthumous offices with added grades even from humble rank, all such cases required temporary imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 至於母後、後族、臣僚，錄其先世，各有等差。

translations.literal: As for empress dowagers, consort clans, and officials—recording their forebears had separate grades.
translations.idiomatic: As for empress dowagers, consort clans, and officials, ennoblement of forebears was graded separately.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后、皇后並贈三世，婕妤二世，貴人止贈其父而已。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and Empress all received three generations; Lady of Handsome Fairness two; Lady of Excellent Worth only their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and Empress all received posthumous ennoblement for three generations; Ladies of Handsome Fairness for two; Ladies of Excellent Worth only for their fathers.

sentences.zh: 宰相、三師、三公、王、尚書令、中書令、侍中、樞密使副、知院、同知院事、參知政事、宣微使、度簽書同簽書樞密院事、觀文殿大學士、節度使，並贈三世。

translations.literal: Chief ministers, Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, kings, Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Chancellery, Palace Attendant, Vice Bureau chief, Bureau director, Associate Bureau director, Vice Grand Councillor, Bureau of Palace Attendants commissioner, Commissioner signing for and Associate Commissioner signing for the Bureau of Military Affairs, Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and military governors—all received three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers, the Three Preceptors, the Three Dukes, kings, the Director of the Secretariat, the Director of the Chancellery, the Palace Attendant, Vice Commissioners and Directors of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Grand Councillors, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, Commissioners signing for the Bureau of Military Affairs, Grand Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and military governors all received posthumous ennoblement for three generations.

sentences.zh: 東宮三師、僕射、留守、節度使、三司使、觀文殿學士、資政殿大學士，並贈二世。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace Three Preceptors, Vice Premiers, territorial governors, military governors, Commissioners of the Three Departments, Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Supporting Governance—all received two generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace Three Preceptors, Vice Premiers, territorial governors, military governors, Commissioners of the Three Departments, Academicians of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and Grand Academicians of the Hall for Supporting Governance all received posthumous ennoblement for two generations.

sentences.zh: 餘官或見任，或致仕，並贈一世。
